title: Is IFTTT Free? Plan Limits and Alternatives (2026)
summary: Is IFTTT free? Yes, but its free plan only handles basic automations and stops working without warning when you hit usage limits.
body_markdown:
## Cost of missed leads on IFTTT


Choosing by feel meant the leads that applet would have routed went nowhere. One of them, at **$47 for a small-business lead** , is worth more than a full month of IFTTT Pro at $7.99.


### Lost leads and hours from applet failure


Because most businesses are already slow, silence is expensive. According to[Harvard Business Review via Callatta](https://guides.callatta.com/playbooks/lead-response-time-research) , only 37% of inbound web leads get a first response within an hour, so two-thirds of prospects are left waiting over sixty minutes to hear back.


Another 16% wait between 1 and 24 hours, by which time most will have moved on. A further 24% wait more than a day, and 23% are never answered at all, per Harvard Business Review via Callatta, which means nearly half your leads are lost.


So **47% of leads get nothing** for a full day or ever, and a stopped applet pushes your leads toward that group without anyone deciding it, which means you silently become a non-responder.


Then there are the hours, the second bill. When the applet stops, someone copies each lead by hand into the tracker or the inbox.


At $35 an hour, according to[Limesdigital](https://limesdigital.com/blog/the-copy-paste-tax-what-manual-data-entry-really-costs-you) , every hour of copying costs $35, and that hour comes out of a person who was supposed to be doing something else. Nobody logs it, so it never shows up as a line item.


### IFTTT Pro cost versus lost leads


Run the arithmetic. Pro at $7.99 divided by $47 per lead is 0.17, so one saved lead pays for about six months of Pro.


Per Limesdigital, Pro divided by $35 per hour is 0.23 of an hour, so roughly 14 minutes of manual copying costs the same as a month of the plan.


The chart sets the outage cost, hours at $35 plus leads at $47, against Pro at $7.99 month-to-month, so a single incident can cost more than the Pro fee you'd save by skipping it for months.


The outage side climbs with every lead and every hour, and the Pro side stays flat.


The upgrade decision is rarely close once you count what the stop costs. The harder question is which limit you'll hit first, and that's what you should write down before you build.
